text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Bomb disposal experts defused a highly powerful explosive device in the 15th district office of the liberal junior government coalition party the Free Democrats on Sunday.

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said on Friday Hungary's probable entry to NATO in the first wave of expansion was a recompense for the country's achievements and suffering during the transformation period.

- Free Democrats president Gabor Kuncze said the party does not support the parliamentary ratification of the agreement concluded with the Vatican as 50 of the properties involved are erroneously featured on the list and the effect of the church financing on the budget is still not clear.

- Socialiist Party parliamentary group leader Imre Szekeres said Friday it was unacceptable that Free Democrat group leader Istvan Szentivanyi should appeal to the Socialist caucus without prior consultations.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said he hoped there would be a fast track for some EU aspirant nations if the EU opens talks simultaneously with all applicants.

- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny said the social security deficit is around 20 million forints while Transport Minister Karoly Lotz said the railway company MAV needs 8-10 billion forints in subsidies to avert aggressive cost-cutting, including job losses.
- Electricity company MVM will invite bids via two large-scale tenders next month for the construction of several power plants.
